claims.claim: Inside an ant colony, millions of tiny workers cooperate like a living superorganism.
claims.evidence: Ant colonies are described as superorganisms
claims.quote: The colonies are described as superorganisms because the ants appear to operate as a unified entity, collectively working together to support the colony.

claims.claim: The colony revolves around one or more egg‑laying queens, whose sole purpose is to lay thousands of eggs.
claims.evidence: Typical colony consists of one or more egg-laying queens
claims.quote: The typical colony consists of one or more egg-laying queens, numerous sterile females (workers, soldiers) and, seasonally, many winged sexual males and females.

claims.claim: From each egg emerges a larva, then a pupa, and finally an adult whose destiny is decided by its nutrition and hormones.
claims.quote: From each egg emerges a larva, then a pupa, and finally an adult whose destiny is decided by its nutrition and hormones.

claims.claim: Most adults become sterile females—workers that tend brood, forage, and defend the nest, while some develop into larger soldiers.
claims.evidence: Typical colonies consist of various castes of sterile, wingless females
claims.quote: Typical colonies consist of various castes of sterile, wingless females, most of which are workers (ergates), as well as soldiers (dinergates) and other specialised groups.

claims.claim: At the right season, the queen also raises winged males and virgin females, called alates, that gather in massive swarms.
claims.evidence: Seasonal production of winged virgin queens and males
claims.quote: A mature ant colony seasonally produces winged virgin queens and males, called alates.

claims.claim: These nuptial flights happen at species‑specific times of day, and the alates leave the nest in search of mates.
claims.evidence: Nuptial flights occur at species-characteristic times of the day
claims.quote: In order to establish new colonies, ants undertake flights that occur at species-characteristic times of the day.

claims.claim: Males die soon after mating, and most females also perish, but a few fertilized queens shed their wings and descend to start new colonies.
claims.evidence: Males die shortly after mating, and most females perish
claims.quote: The males die shortly thereafter, along with most of the females. A small percentage of the females survive to initiate new nests.

claims.claim: The new queen digs a small chamber, lays her first eggs, and the cycle begins anew, linking countless generations beneath the soil.
claims.evidence: New queen starts a new colony
claims.quote: The new queen digs a small chamber, lays her first eggs, and the cycle begins anew, linking countless generations beneath the soil.

claims.claim: From a single egg to a sprawling underground metropolis, the ant colony reminds us that cooperation can build worlds.
claims.evidence: Universally established fact about cooperation in ant colonies
